text: Read carefully the article about celebrities and their influence on people which is in the
Reading Booklet Insert. Then answer Section 1, Question 1 on this Question Paper.
Write a letter to the journalist, in which you discuss what he has to say about
You may agree or disagree with the journalist’s views.
• identify and evaluate the journalist’s views
• use your own ideas to support your comments on the journalist’s views.
Base your letter on what you have read in the article but be careful to use your own words.
Write between 1½ and 2 sides, allowing for the size of your handwriting.
Up to 10 marks are available for the content of your answer, and up to 15 marks for the
Write about 2 sides, allowing for the size of your handwriting, on one of the following questions.
Up to 13 marks are available for the content of your answer, and up to 12 marks are available for
the style and accuracy of your writing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘In a few years’ time, the books we love and cherish will be replaced by flat, grey, electronic
texts.’ Give your views on this statement.
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Are teenagers today free to express themselves as individuals?
Descriptive Writing

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
You come across a puppet show being performed to a crowd of children in the town square.
Describe what you see and hear, and the atmosphere around you.
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe a shopping trip through a bazaar, spice market or souk in which you stop, at
least twice, to consider buying an item. Describe how this experience excites your senses
throughout.
Narrative Writing

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Write a story entitled ‘The Watcher’.
OR

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘As I was about to knock on the heavy oak door, a booming voice commanded “Enter!” and
stopped me in my tracks.’ Use this quotation at some point in your story.
